name: Siavash Mahdavi

education.notes: 3-year UK BEng in mechatronics — same generalist hard-engineering foundation as a Mechatronic Eng undergrad today.
Pre-deep-learning era MSc — statistical, evolutionary and symbolic AI, not neural networks. Context matters when comparing to today's ML MScs.
Doctoral research applied evolutionary algorithms to robotic systems / structural design — directly seeded the generative-design IP at Within Technologies.

keyDecisions: Chose mechatronics over pure CS or mechanical — the cross-domain hardware+software foundation became the recurring through-line of every later venture.
lessons: Mechatronics is a high-optionality undergraduate degree — it keeps doors open to robotics, AI, hardware and pure-software paths simultaneously.
London-cluster universities (King's, UCL, Imperial) form one tight academic ecosystem; staying inside it for 8 years compounded local network value.
careerSteps.notes: Web era; AI was an academic backwater. Choosing this stack in 1998 was a long-duration bet, not a hot field.

careerSteps.role: MSc then PhD researcher (Intelligent Systems → Evolutionary Robotics)
keyDecisions: Stacked MSc Intelligent Systems → PhD Evolutionary Robotics — five additional years of deep technical specialisation post-BEng.
Picked a PhD topic (evolutionary / generative algorithms for physical systems) that doubled as a directly commercialisable IP base.
Stayed in London for the entire academic chain — built a long-running UCL network that later paid back via dealflow and the Honorary Lecturer post.
lessons: PhD research is highest-leverage when the topic is directly productisable in a vertical that pays for physics (aerospace, medtech).
Heavy upfront technical depth (PhD-level) can be re-applied across multiple verticals — design, manufacturing, music — across decades.
Long single-city academic tenure produces compounding local network value that pure mobility doesn't.
careerSteps.notes: Pre-deep-learning era; ML at UCL in 2001-02 was statistical/evolutionary. The thesis itself became the spin-out IP for Within.

keyDecisions: Spun a generative-design company out of PhD research ~2 years post-doctorate (founded 2008) — used the gap to refine commercial application of evolutionary algorithms for aerospace / medtech.
Targeted high-value niches early: aerospace lattice components, customised running shoes, orthopaedic implants — verticals that already valued physics-driven design.
Sold Within to Autodesk in 2014 — exit-via-strategic-acquirer rather than scale-to-IPO; ~6 years from founding to exit.
Briefly stayed at Autodesk as Senior Director / Future of Making leading their generative-design integration.
lessons: PhD-to-startup conversion works when the research is directly productisable and the target customer already pays for the underlying physics — most PhDs do not pass this test.
Strategic acquirers (Autodesk) pay for category-defining tech in adjacent verticals — a viable European exit path that does not require IPO-scale revenue.
Spending a brief post-acquisition stint inside the acquirer is how you understand how strategic M&A actually values technology — useful for the next venture.
careerSteps.notes: Within Technologies founded 2008 (Companies House / Crunchbase); Autodesk acquired Within in 2014; specific deal value not publicly disclosed. This is the load-bearing turning point: research → product → strategic exit, all in one chapter.

keyDecisions: Co-founded a sister company focused on mass-customisation of consumer products — ran in parallel to Within.
Raised seed funding from EOS, a major industrial 3D-printing player — strategic rather than purely financial backing.
lessons: Running parallel ventures off a shared technical core (generative design + 3D printing) is plausible when the underlying IP is reusable across applications.
Industrial strategics (EOS) writing seed cheques is a European-specific funding route under-used by software founders.
careerSteps.notes: Less prominent than Within; consumer-mass-customisation thesis was early and largely did not scale at the time.

keyDecisions: Co-founded AI Music in London with Inderjit Birdee and Andy Khavand — porting the generative playbook from physical (3D-printed parts) to media (adaptive music).
Raised ~$7.16M across two rounds; reported peak valuation ~£17.6M.
Acqui-hired by Apple in early 2022 — second strategic-acquirer exit in eight years.
lessons: Second-time founders compound by re-applying the same playbook (generative AI) across domains — domain knowledge is the cheaper-to-acquire half of the equation.
Acqui-hire by a FAANG is a credible European founder outcome — not unicorn money, but team-and-tech validation worth ~7-figures per founder.
Stable co-founder teams matter: Birdee + Khavand recur in Ossia Studio — durable trust beats fresh team-building each time.
careerSteps.notes: Apple acquisition publicly reported by FT/Music Business Worldwide in February 2022. Deal value not disclosed.

keyDecisions: Took a partner role at Newlab — Brooklyn-based frontier-tech studio/venture group — extending into deep-tech investing alongside operating.
lessons: Founders with credible deep-tech exits get recruited into venture/operator-partner seats, which compound network access for their next ventures.
Investor seats run in parallel to operating roles; they are not necessarily a retirement step.
careerSteps.notes: Role appears part-time alongside operating ventures.

keyDecisions: Maintained formal academic affiliation post-PhD as Honorary Lecturer at UCL.
lessons: Keeping an academic affiliation is low-cost and feeds back into both dealflow (student founders) and credibility with deep-tech LPs.

keyDecisions: Re-teamed with AI Music co-founders Andy Khavand and Inderjit Birdee post-Apple acquisition for a new venture in generative AI for creative tooling.
lessons: Stable founding teams across multiple ventures (Birdee + Khavand here) are a recurring pattern in serial-founder success.
Post-acqui-hire, the same team re-spinning out within 1-2 years is a recognisable pattern in London's AI cluster.
careerSteps.notes: Early-stage; thesis appears to be generative AI applied to creative tooling.

exitEvents.notes: Within Technologies (founded 2008) acquired by Autodesk in 2014. Deal value not disclosed.
AI Music acqui-hired by Apple. Deal value not disclosed.

outcomes.currentStatus: Serial AI/deep-tech founder based in London; Co-founder & CEO of Ossia Studio, Partner at Newlab, UCL Honorary Lecturer, and angel investor.

lessons.lesson: Re-apply deep technical foundations (AI, robotics, generative methods) across multiple domains — design, manufacturing, music — to ride successive technology waves rather than betting on a single one.
European deep-tech founders can realistically exit via strategic acquirer (Autodesk, Apple) rather than IPO — set funding and burn expectations accordingly.
lessons.source: inferred from Within and AI Music exits

lessons.lesson: Hold the same co-founder team across multiple ventures where possible; Birdee/Khavand recurring across AI Music → Ossia is not an accident.
PhD-to-startup is a credible European path when the thesis IP has a direct vertical buyer — but only if the founder treats the doctorate as product spec, not as pure research.

notes: AI-era serial founder with deep technical (PhD Evolutionary Robotics) background; arc is directly applicable to a BEng Mechatronic Eng → ML/AI path. The load-bearing move is PhD-thesis-as-startup-IP (Within), repeated as playbook-port (AI Music). Caveat: an earlier research brief identified him as a Wordsmith co-founder, but public sources consistently list Wordsmith's founders as Ross McNairn, Robbie Falkenthal and Volodymyr Giginiak — Mahdavi's link to Wordsmith could not be verified and may be an error or undisclosed advisor role.

firstCompany.oneLiner: Generative-design / 3D-printing software spun out of his UCL PhD in evolutionary robotics. Targeted aerospace lattice components, custom running shoes, orthopaedic implants. Acquired by Autodesk in 2014.

preFounderRoles.notes: 3-year UK BEng — same generalist hard-engineering foundation as a Mechatronic Eng undergrad today.
Pre-deep-learning era MSc — statistical, evolutionary and symbolic AI.
Doctoral research applied evolutionary algorithms to robotic systems / structural design — directly seeded Within's IP.

nowSummary: Serial AI/deep-tech founder; Co-founder & CEO of Ossia Studio (2022+), Partner at Newlab, UCL Honorary Lecturer. Two strategic-acquirer exits (Autodesk 2014, Apple acqui-hired AI Music 2022; values undisclosed).
